editorial:
Top Hat is RKO Radio Pictures' 1935 musical, directed by Mark Sandrich, with Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers and songs by Irving Berlin. It premiered on August 29, 1935 at Radio City Music Hall in New York and was released across the United States the following week. It was RKO's most profitable film of the 1930s and was chosen for the National Film Registry in 1990. A creator would want it for the dance numbers and Berlin's songs, but the film is not a clear public-domain candidate.

The rights trap is that no non-renewal could be shown. This dossier found no renewal record and did not open a Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volume. The film also sits on a 1911 Hungarian play, Berlin's separate song copyrights and Max Steiner's score, and Universal and Warner issued restored DVDs. Do not treat any copy as free to reuse until a renewal-volume check is done.
faq: Is Top Hat (1935) in the public domain in the US?
Not established. The film was published in 1935, so it is not free by term alone. No renewal search was completed here. Check the 1962–1964 renewal volumes before reusing it.
Can I use the songs or a restored DVD copy?

Not safely. The songs are by Irving Berlin and Max Steiner supervised the orchestration, and the status of neither was checked. The Universal (2003) and Warner (2005) restored releases carry added material such as an introduction and commentary. Ripping a copy-protected disc can also break the DMCA (17 U.S.C. 1201).
